workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer says the cardholder cancelled their FluxFit Online subscription on 18 March 2025 and was still charged GBP 29.99 on 20 April 2025. To defend, the merchant must prove all four of the following: its terms disclosed the recurring billing and how to cancel; the cardholder was notified of the upcoming charge in advance (where the amount is over the threshold); there is no record of a cancellation request before the billing date; and the cardholder originally opted in to recurring billing.

pointers.quote:
Subscriptions auto-renew
monthly at the rate disclosed at signup until cancelled. Members may cancel at any time via their
account dashboard or by emailing support@fluxfit.example.

requirements.reasoning: The terms disclose monthly auto-renewal and two cancellation methods (dashboard or email). They show what the terms say, not that this cardholder saw or accepted this version; that question belongs to requirement 4.

pointers.quote: Members will be notified by email at least 5 days prior to each renewal.

requirements.reasoning: This is a policy statement only, not proof that a pre-renewal email was sent to this cardholder before 20 April 2025. The stated 5-day notice is also shorter than the typical 7-day expectation. It has not been confirmed whether GBP 29.99 is over the applicable threshold.
No account log, cancellation history or support-mailbox record was supplied to show that no cancellation was submitted on or around 18 March 2025, which is the core of the cardholder's claim.
There is no signup record, checkbox acceptance log or confirmation email showing the cardholder opted in to recurring billing. The generic terms document does not prove acceptance by this cardholder.

workup.action_justification: Only one of four required elements is satisfied; the missing items are system records the merchant should be able to pull, so the case is not yet lost.
evidence_to_request: Account activity and cancellation log for the cardholder's FluxFit account covering 1 March to 20 April 2025, showing no cancellation was submitted via the dashboard
A search of the support@fluxfit.example mailbox and ticketing system for any message from the cardholder's email address between 1 March and 20 April 2025, with the search criteria stated
Original signup record: date and time, IP address, cardholder email, the terms version accepted, and the recurring-billing consent checkbox or confirmation screen
Signup or welcome confirmation email sent to the cardholder disclosing the recurring charge
Copy of the pre-renewal notification email for the 20 April 2025 charge, with send timestamp, recipient address and delivery log
Billing history for the subscription showing prior renewal dates and amounts
The version of the terms in force on the cardholder's signup date, if signup was before February 2025
workup.rationale: The cardholder states the FluxFit Online subscription was cancelled on 18 March 2025 and disputes the GBP 29.99 renewal charged on 20 April 2025. The merchant's terms (terms_v3.2) disclose monthly auto-renewal and cancellation via the account dashboard or by email to support. The file contains no record of the cardholder's original opt-in, no proof that a pre-renewal notification was sent, and no account or support log showing an absence of a cancellation request before the billing date. Representment is on hold pending those records from the merchant.
caveats: The terms were published in February 2025. If the cardholder signed up earlier, the version accepted at signup may differ and must be supplied.

The terms promise 5 days' notice before renewal, which is below the typical 7-day advance-notice expectation. Even with proof of sending, requirement 2 may be weak if the amount is over the threshold.

The 'cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing period' clause does not help the merchant. A cancellation on 18 March would take effect before the 20 April renewal, so the defence depends entirely on proving no cancellation was received.
AVS Y, CVV M and frictionless 3DS relate to the original authentication. They do not address whether the subscription was cancelled and carry little weight under 13.2.
The transaction timestamp of 00:00:01Z is consistent with an automated renewal. Confirm that the renewal date aligns with the cardholder's billing cycle.
No IP address or device fingerprint is on the transaction record, so the opt-in must be proven from the merchant's own signup logs.

rule_text:
Visa 13.2 - Cancelled Recurring Transaction
Issuer claim: Cardholder cancelled a recurring subscription but was still charged.
Logic: ALL 4 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. Terms of service disclosing the recurring billing arrangement and the cancellation method
  2. Evidence the cardholder was notified of the upcoming charge (typically 7+ days in advance) for transactions over a defined threshold
  3. No record of the cardholder having submitted a cancellation request prior to the billing date
  4. Evidence of the cardholder's original opt-in to the recurring arrangement
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: frictionless
Shipping vs billing postcode: no shipping postcode on file (digital goods or service)
Chargeback raised 15 days after the transaction
